experiments.title: C1 campaign — RFdiffusion3 mini-proteins
experiments.summary: 57 designs folded, 31 two-domain samples. The reach across groove and junction exists; activation stays unproven.
experiments.goal: Design mini-proteins that bind the GLP1R extracellular domain AND the ECD-TMD junction — the pose that activation needs.
goal_extra: Answers: does a de-novo mini-protein reach both sub-sites at once?
Answers: which hotspot set gives the best two-domain rate?
experiments.verdict_detail: Junction-only hotspots beat groove+junction for two-domain reach (25% vs 14%). Best design e1-r0025 spans groove, junction, TM top and ECL3.

experiments.title: C2 campaign — EvoBind cyclic peptides
experiments.summary: 15 designs folded. The length sweep: 15 aa is the sweet spot (3 hits, ipSAE 0.83-0.88); 12 aa and 20 aa produced none.
experiments.goal: Cyclic peptides at the orthosteric site — the modality whose published designs activated GLP1R in cAMP assays.
goal_extra: Answers: which peptide length engages the groove+junction?
Answers: does an independent peptide tool reach the site at all?
experiments.verdict_detail: Three 15-aa peptides in the submission band; the 12-aa and 20-aa runs produced no two-domain designs.

experiments.title: C3 campaign — BoltzGen cyclic peptides
experiments.summary: 55 designs screened across four batches, 9 two-domain samples. The junction constraint transfers from campaign 1.
experiments.goal: A second peptide generator at the same site, with its own scoring suite — orthogonal candidates and a cross-check on the c1/c2 winners.
goal_extra: Answers: does BoltzGen produce two-domain designs at the junction?
Answers: do two independent pipelines agree on the same designs?
experiments.verdict_detail: Seven two-domain hits across the four batches. Key lesson: BoltzGen's own metrics ranked its best designs wrongly — every design must pass the independent screen.

experiments.title: C6 campaign — SolubleMPNN re-sequencing
experiments.summary: 40 re-sequenced designs, 20 two-domain samples. The challenge's best design: ipSAE 0.934 with the full groove.
experiments.goal: Re-sequence campaign 1's champion backbones with SolubleMPNN, interface-pinned - the fix for ProteinMPNN's alanine collapse.
goal_extra: Answers: does a better sequence model lift the c1 backbones?
experiments.verdict_detail: The retry worked: one backbone produced a family better than the original on affinity, groove coverage and reach.

experiments.title: C7 campaign — extended-length peptides (20-24 aa)
experiments.summary: 18 designs at 20-24 aa, 5 two-domain HITs. Viable, not superior to 15-18 aa.
experiments.goal: The one untried length class at the junction site.
goal_extra: Answers: does a longer peptide beat the 15-18 aa band?
experiments.verdict_detail: Longer peptides cover more groove (two touch all six residues) but do not beat 15-18 aa on affinity (best 0.834 vs 0.934).

experiments.title: C8 campaign — deep junction at scale
experiments.summary: 60 designs repeating the c3 junction recipe, 14 two-domain samples and 3 designs with the full 6/6 activation pharmacophore.
experiments.goal: Repeat the exact configuration that produced the most complete activation geometries, at 60-design scale.
goal_extra: Answers: does the c3 yield hold at scale?
Answers: how many 6/6 activation geometries does one batch give?
experiments.verdict_detail: The yield held: three more 6/6 designs, including c8-run13 - a two-domain HIT with the full pharmacophore. The activation pool is now nine designs.
